item.title: GTA 6 Is Getting Review Bombed in Zelda vs. GTA Troll War
item.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time fans are fighting over Metacritic scores as part of a larger anti-woke culture war.
item.text:
Grand Theft Auto 6 may be the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic, and may have earned a record-breaking $3.79 billion on launch day, but that doesn't mean Rockstar Games' new blockbuster can't have its haters. Multiple groups have descended on GTA 6's Metacritic page to attack the game for its perceived shortcomings, much of that criticism is based on culture war nonsense.
But some of GTA 6's detractors are targeting the game for another reason: for slighting The Legend of Zelda.
GTA 6 made its debut on Metacritic with a 99 Metascore, based on more than 150 critics reviews. That feat nudged the previous best game of all time, at least going by Metacritic score averages, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, down to No. 2 on the review aggregator website. That has led some Legend of Zelda supporters to review bomb Grand Theft Auto 6 on Metacritic, and some GTA 6 supporters to do the same to Zelda. Now, both camps are in a pointless war to lower the other franchise's user review score.
Over the past few days, GTA and Zelda fans have been trading barbs and slinging "0" user review scores at their perceived rivals. As of Sunday, Nov. 22, Grand Theft Auto 6's user review score on Metacritic has dipped to 5.6, indicating "mixed or average" reviews from players. In response, the original Ocarina of Time and its Nintendo Switch 2 remake have also been review bombed (though their user scores are in the mid-8s as of Sunday).
The completion percentage is the only tally GTA keeps, and for you it is the whole reason the hours are worth counting.
Your first hour goes on the collectibles menu, working out the size of the job before you start it.
A mission that goes wrong gets replayed until it is clean, because there is a rating attached and you are going for it.
You were still at 68 percent when the credits rolled, and the credits did not feel like an ending.
GTA spends more effort on the feel of a car at night than on almost anything else, and you are the player that work was for.
There is a waypoint on your map and you may never reach it, because the drive is better than the arrival.
You have one car, you drive it everywhere, and you know exactly where you parked it.
The credits rolled and nothing changed. You are still out there with the radio on.
Stopping at a red light in an empty city is a choice nobody asks you to make, which is exactly why you make it.

item.title: GTA 6's T-shirts Are True Works of Art
item.summary: Fashion can help you evade police in GTA 6, and Rockstar's design team has crafted some seriously covetable threads for the game.
item.text:
We've known for some time that fashion would be a big deal in Grand Theft Auto 6. In Rockstar's official promotional materials for the game, both Jason and Lucia were prominently featured wearing stylish clothing, from Lucia's body-hugging gold dress to Jason's slick Miami Vice-inspired aqua sport coat. Even supporting characters like Brian wear Tommy Bahama-inspired aloha shirts yanked straight from the closet of a dapper middle-aged stoner. GTA 6 has drawn praise from all quarters for its scrupulous attention to detail in every aspect of the game, and there's one area the developer went far, far harder than it needed to: the vast and immaculate selection of T-shirts.
Having a diverse wardrobe isn't just a fun little customization touch in GTA 6. If you're reported for committing a crime in Leonida — and this will happen very often — police will be able to recognize you based on your car, your physical appearance, and what you're wearing. Keeping a couple spare outfits in your trunk or hastily buying a new ensemble on the run can be the difference between a successful job and ending up busted (or wasted).
I'm taking my time with GTA 6 and still kicking around the introductory area of Key Lento. I know I should be putting money in my family savings account. It would probably be in my best interest to learn how to drive without sideswiping semi-trucks or taking out stop signs. Perhaps I ought to be buying more guns. Instead, I'm trawling South Leonida for all the vintage and souvenir shops I can find. You can keep your fancy cars. I've got a T-shirt collection to maintain.
Much like in real life, you never know when you're going to find a gem in a vintage boutique or souvenir shop in GTA 6. My prized Rusty Anchor shirt came from an optional mission where you take Cal for drinks, he has a few too many, and you have to take him home. item.title: GTA 6 needed a dedicated team to make sure all its different body types could share animations: 'It was a huge team effort'
item.summary: Making sure your animations don't break while you're cultivating mass.
item.text:
We don't know precisely how big GTA 6's "big boy" budget was, but let's put aside the alarming excess of contemporary mass-consumption entertainment for a moment and talk about the real big boy: bulked up Jason.
While GTA 6's body morphing might not go quite as far (in terms of waistband measurements) as its predecessor San Andreas—or even a game like Fable 2—it does boast extensive variety of different body shapes among its cast, and making that work at such a high level of visual fidelity took an entire dedicated team.
In an interview with IGN, Rockstar vice president of animation Mark Tennant said it was an early decision in development to "push the variation in character sizes and body types … This required us to establish a very robust way to share animations between characters while still resolving multiple points of contact, such as most vehicle interactions and grappling in hand-to-hand combat."
It also took eschewing a "traditional approach" in favor of "new techniques," the sort I imagine you can only implement at Rockstar levels of budget and manpower. "We also had to grow a team dedicated to overseeing the implementation, which required close collaboration with the art and rigging teams," said Tennant. "All these aspects needed to come together to make it work, so it was a huge team effort."
In the same IGN piece, senior technical art director Valmor Garcia said the ultimate goal was to ensure each character had "singular awareness and visual identities," which included giving them unique faces and anatomy (the six-figure animation count is part of that too, I imagine). All the blood, sweat, and so on seem to be paying off given the game's absolutely massive launch, but Saints Row 3 is still the only crime sandbox that lets me replace all my character's dialog with meaningless zombie grunts, so it's impossible to say which is better.

item.title: Sorry, Vice City, but You’re the Most Boring Part of GTA 6
item.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6's map is so well-designed that Vice City just might be the least exciting thing about Leonida.
item.text:
When Grand Theft Auto 6 was first announced, fans were thrilled at the prospect of returning to Vice City. The Miami-inspired location has always been one of the series’ most memorable locations, its neon-lit streets standing in contrast to the grittiness of Liberty City. While I was as excited as anyone to go clubbing and spend some time on the beach, after 70 hours, GTA 6 has struck me with one surprise thought: Vice City is the least interesting part of Leonida.
I don’t mean to say that Vice City sucks — far from it! It’s an immaculately designed video game city with more environmental diversity in any given corner than some open-world games fit into an entire map. The fact that it’s one of my least favorite places to spend time is more a testament to every other location in GTA 6’s Florida-inspired world. From small towns to the deep wilderness, every corner of Leonida is a delight to discover because every area feels so different.
I blame GTA 6’s opening chapter for spoiling me rotten. Jason and Lucia’s story begins in the Leonida Keys, a brilliantly constructed introductory area that I fell in love with instantly. As someone who is fascinated by the Florida Keys, the real islands that the location is based on, I was thrilled to find a digital space that so accurately captured a genuinely surreal part of America. The real Keys feel like an isolated nation, densely packing stores and suburbs onto narrow islands. The Leonida Keys feel both like an idyllic vacation hideaway and a mundane suburb, which gives GTA 6’s opening chapter such a distinct feel from the rest of the game. The small town nature of it makes for one of my favorite chunks of any GTA game.
Even after getting out of the Leonida Keys, it’s still a while before you get to Vice City. First, Jason and Lucia spend a stint upstate hopping around some small towns separated by vast farmland. Port Gellhorn has the feel of an industrial town, the kind of place that’s lined with used car lots. Some great action set pieces come out of that setup; one time I busted up a well-guarded abandoned bowling alley and wound up in a gritty gang shootout.
Way south of there, you’ll find Capri, another highlight. The squeaky-clean upper-class town is full of boutique clothing stores and high-end cafes. When Jason and Lucia arrive there, they are immediately profiled by street cops who clock them as poor outsiders who don’t belong in town. item.title: Rockstar Says Darts Were Cut From GTA 6 Because It Didn't Have 'Unlimited Money or Time' to Make It 'Feel Proper'
item.summary: Rockstar Games crammed a lot of content into GTA 6, but fan-favorite mini-games like darts and bowling didn't make the cut because the team didn't have "unlimited money or unlimited time" to do those activities justice.
item.text:
Rockstar Games crammed a lot of content into GTA 6, but fan-favorite mini-games like darts and bowling didn't make the cut because the team didn't have "unlimited money or unlimited time" to do those activities justice.
Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson explained why the studio chose to focus on some aspects of development and not others during an interview with VGC. As noted by the site, picking up a game of darts has proven to be a good pastime in games like GTA 5 and GTA Online, but in GTA 6, the standards were a bit higher.
From NPCs to the feel of motorized scooters, Leonida is Rockstar's most realistic playground yet. Every blade of grass was given special attention, and while pool was one game the team was able to fully realize, not everything panned out like they had hoped. Nelson said "darts was a contentious one" when talking about the decision to cut it from the game, explaining that it was left behind because the team didn't have the resources to do it right.
"Even we… you hear they have unlimited money or unlimited time, even we do not and so sometimes you just have to admit we are not going to be able to make this to the level we feel we need to," he said.
Nelson elaborated, saying that, starting with Red Dead Redemption 2, the team started to treat mini-games more like activities. In other words, bonuses like darts became less about being a diversion of Rockstar's open worlds and more of an extension of them. The goal is to make pool, darts, or any other activity feel like it's just as punchy and weighty for Jason and Lucia as it is in the real world.
Using GTA 6's in-game workouts as an example, he added, "You’re not just pushing a button; it mimics what weightlifting is."
"A lot of work [is needed] to get it tuned right," Nelson continued. "Darts is one we just didn’t get to."
Long story short, Rockstar just "didn't have the resources" to make it "feel proper." His thoughts on the matter – or any scenario where a mechanic or activity is cut – were summed up in one line: "It’s better not to do it than to do it and have it not be good enough."
GTA 6 is now the highest-rated game of all time. IGN gave it a 10/10 review.

item.title: iShowSpeed Rushed GTA 6 and Got a Bad Ending
item.summary: Changing your ending in Grand Theft Auto VI means loading an earlier save, and iShowSpeed accidentally overwrote his 98% save trying to do just that.
item.text:
Grand Theft Auto VI is only a few days old and iShowSpeed has already finished it with an ending he didn’t want. iShowSpeed played the main story in a single 52-hour marathon with no sleep, starting the night of November 18 and signing off on November 20. The ending left him in tears after he broke his own promise to pace himself. Then he accidentally overwrote a 98 percent save while trying for a different ending because he didn't like what happened to Jason and Lucia at the end.
Interestingly, Speed said before launch he would not marathon GTA VI, planning 10 to 12 hour days so his viewers could play along at their own pace. Once the game unlocked though, he never got off. The total run lasted roughly 52 hours and 31 minutes, with no sleep in three days by his own count. Around the 43-hour mark his PlayStation 5 crashed mid-cutscene and he feared his progress was gone, until an autosave pulled him back. He kept pushing to the credits.
Impressive stamina, sure, but is it a smart way to experience the biggest open world Rockstar Games has ever built? Not quite.
In his own short "I BEAT GTA 6!" he reaches an outcome he clearly was not ready for and falls apart, asking over and over what he just watched. We will not tell you what happens. What matters is that GTA 6 does not have a single ending. Rockstar has confirmed there are a lot more than two and which one you get depends on choices you make across the whole story and Speed got the ending shaped by his choices.
Then came the part that should make every player wince. Trying to reload a 98 percent save to chase a different ending, he overwrote the wrong file and lost it. He never got to see the other versions. This is exactly where our coverage of the new save system matters, because GTA 6 will not let you replay story missions the way older games did. Your choices stick. If you blitz the story half-asleep and reach an ending you hate, you cannot just hop back a mission to redo it.
Speed found that out at the worst possible moment and in the most heartbreaking way possible.
None of this is a knock on Speed, who gave his viewers a wild three days. It is a knock on the idea that you should race this game. We said before launch to take the day after launch off, not launch day itself and this is a good reason to have listened to us. item.title: Звезда Red Dead Redemption 2 стала кастинг-директором GTA VI — она нашла девушку для обложки игры
item.summary: Для одной из актрис сотрудничество с Rockstar Games вышло на новый уровень.
item.text:
Для одной из актрис сотрудничество с Rockstar Games вышло на новый уровень.
Недавно состоялся релиз Grand Theft Auto VI и спало действие NDA (соглашения о неразглашении). Актёры и другие участники проекта стали подтверждать своё участие.
Как оказалось, команду Rockstar Games пополнила актриса, которая в прошлом сыграла одного из персонажей в Red Dead Redemption 2. Кали Элизабет Мур (Cali Elizabeth Moore), которую игроки знают по роли Эбигейл Робертс, стала кастинг-директором Grand Theft Auto VI.
Она опубликовала обращение в социальной сети:
После многих лет работы с Rockstar в качестве актрисы в Red Dead Redemption 2 у меня появилась возможность стать штатным сотрудником компании —кастинг-директором Rockstar, и я с радостью ухватилась за шанс работать с этой замечательной, доброй и талантливой командой. После многих лет кастинга тысяч актёров со всего мира для этого проекта я невероятно горжусь тем, чего добилась моя потрясающая команда. Провести бесчисленные часы в поисках актёра, свободно говорящего с нужным испанским акцентом; танцовщицы для необходимой анимации в стриптиз-клубе; актёра, достойного наших блестяще написанных главных персонажей; каскадёра, способного выполнить захватывающий дух трюк; идеального аутентичного лица для сканирования — это была огромная задача, и так здорово наконец поделиться этой работой со всем миром.
После выхода также стало известно о том, кто на самом деле стал прототипом девушки с обложки Grand Theft Auto VI. Недавно актриса поблагодарила Кали Элизабет Мур и её команду за то, что они нашли её и дали шанс принять участие в таком проекте.

item.summary: Студии пришлось найти баланс между действиями игрока, реакцией партнёра и развитием отношений Джейсона и Люсии.
item.text:
Студии пришлось найти баланс между действиями игрока, реакцией партнёра и развитием отношений Джейсона и Люсии.
Поскольку GTA VI сочетает криминальный боевик с историей любви, физическая близость и романтические отношения занимают в ней заметное место. Rockstar стремилась сделать их естественными и связать с решениями игрока.
Вице-президент Rockstar по анимации Марк Теннант в интервью рассказал:
Изучение физических отношений между Джейсоном и Люсией потребовало долгих размышлений и многочисленных доработок.
Нам нужно было позволить игрокам взаимодействовать с партнёром естественно и с любовью, а развитие отношений должно было правдоподобно зависеть от того, сколько внимания игрок им уделяет.
Романтическая линия не развивается по единому сценарию. В зависимости от решений игрока Джейсон и Люсия могут испытывать сильную страсть друг к другу или оставаться просто напарниками по преступлениям. Поэтому анимации физической близости должны соответствовать текущему состоянию их отношений.
Нам пришлось создать анимации, которые обеспечивают реалистичный баланс между свободой действий игрока и реакцией партнёра, сохраняя при этом весёлый, страстный и приятный характер взаимодействия.

item.title: How to Find and Keep Dom's Charger in GTA 6
item.summary: Find Dom’s Charger lookalike behind a house in Grayson, respray it black and keep it with Moses’s free first registration in Chapter 2.
item.text:
We went hunting through the northern side of Grand Theft Auto VI and found the one car every Fast & Furious fan has been waiting for. Tucked behind a house in Grayson is a rusted, supercharged muscle car that is Dom Toretto's black 1970 Dodge Charger R/T in everything but the badge. Rockstar Games never says the words, but the blower punched through the hood, the drag-strip setting and the classic silhouette leave little doubt about the homage. Best of all, it is free.
Here is exactly where to find it, how to make it look like the movie car and how to keep it for good.
The car is a Bravado Driveshaft Gauntlet, a standout version of the '69 Bravado Gauntlet Custom that the game tags as DriveShaft Famous.
Strip away the fictional brand and you have a 1960s muscle coupe with a supercharger blower standing proud of the hood, the single detail that turns a rusty classic into an unmistakable Charger stand-in from the famous. It is not the same as the modern, Challenger-style Hellfire Gauntlet you will have to find yourself chasing for Randy later.
This one is all American muscle, just like the car Dom had in the The Fast and the Furious, right down to the stance.
Head to Grayson, a town up in Lummox County in the northern of Leonida. The car sits abandoned behind a house that belongs to a local named Sid Thompson, close to a Pay 'n' Spray, a gas station and the train station. The railroad tracks running past the property recall the final drag race from the 2001 film. You cannot miss the car once you are on the right street, it is the only rusted, light-blue muscle coupe with a blower sticking out of the hood.
Scan the car with WAiNK before you touch it, the same way we do in our vehicle theft guide. In our runs, it has no tracker to deal with. Getting in is easy, this is not a locked-down supercar, so you can take it early without a Key Cloner.
Drive it straight out, rusty, faded light-blue paint and all.
There is a Pay 'n' Spray right there in Grayson. Pull in, pick black and the faded blue disappears under Dom's exact color. The respray also does double duty, since it clears the car's description if you picked up any heat grabbing it. A fresh black coat is the difference between a rusty curiosity and the car from the poster.

item.title: Секрет успеха GTA VI: тысяча сотрудников Rockstar работают в студии уже больше 10 лет
item.summary: Около тысячи сотрудников Rockstar Games работают в студии не менее 10 лет, а накопленный опыт ветеранов стал одним из секретов успеха GTA VI.
item.text:
Около тысячи сотрудников Rockstar Games работают в студии не менее 10 лет, а накопленный опыт ветеранов стал одним из секретов успеха GTA VI.
Представительница Rockstar Games рассказала в интервью, что 21% сотрудников компании связаны со студией как минимум десятилетие. Это примерно 1000 человек. Над GTA VI работали многие создатели Red Dead Redemption 2 и предыдущих игр Rockstar.
В октябре компания сообщила, что после выхода Red Dead Redemption 2 штат вырос с 2441 до 4711 человек. Масштаб производства GTA 6 потребовал даже создания специальной команды, которая занималась написанием реплик для безымянных NPC.
Большой штат и опыт сотрудников должны помочь Rockstar быстрее выпускать следующие игры. В студии надеются, что после GTA VI фанатам не придётся ждать очередного проекта так долго.
Движок, инструменты и команда, которые мы создали в ходе работы над этим проектом, позволят нам действовать быстрее.
Grand Theft Auto VI вышла 19 ноября на PS5 и Xbox Series X/S. Игра уже принесла огромную выручку, установив новый рекорд во всей индустрии развлечений. Высокие оценки критиков также подтвердили успех проекта.
